DisplayName: AI-assisted change delivery with guarded delegation
Summary: Structure work so AI agents can assist delivery through bounded delegation, prompt packaging, evaluation, safety review, merge control, and evidence-rich trace capture.
ValueStatement: Gain AI-delivery speed without losing human accountability, evidence quality, safety boundaries, or the ability to audit how a change was produced.
CustomerName: Engineering, AI governance, and release stakeholders
InterfaceContractSummary: Change demand, delegation boundaries, prompts, execution traces, evaluation evidence, safety reviews, and human approvals are combined into one guarded delivery contract.
GovernanceNotes: AI execution is never treated as magic labor. Delegation scope, refusal boundaries, allowed artifacts, evaluation criteria, and merge authority remain explicit and typed.
ChangeSummary: Built by merging SSDF, SSDF-AI, SAMM governance, SLSA provenance thinking, and practical prompt/evaluation control patterns for agent orchestration.
GovernancePolicySummary: Delegated work requires explicit task decomposition, prompt package, output evaluation, safety review, provenance trace, and human merge approval.
ConstitutionRuleSummary: No AI-generated change may enter protected branches or production lanes without human understanding of scope, evidence, and residual risk.
OperatingModeSummary: Guarded autonomy: agents may generate drafts and execute bounded tasks, but humans own delegation boundaries, acceptance, safety, and merge decisions.
SimulationReadinessSummary: Designed specifically for AI-agent orchestration, with enough structure to drive delegated task runners, evaluators, reviewers, and post-hoc audits.
Metrics: Rate of AI outputs accepted without rework
Evidence completeness score per delegated change
Number of blocked changes due to unsafe delegation or weak evaluation
Risks: Delegation scope is too broad and exceeds evidence or safety boundaries.
Prompts and tool permissions are not packaged reproducibly.
Evaluation evidence is weak or unrepresentative.
Merge decisions rely on output polish rather than verified correctness.
TailoringRules: For low-risk documentation changes, simplify benchmark depth but keep trace capture.
For code touching auth, billing, or data boundaries, require mandatory security and model-risk review.
For non-code outputs, keep the same delegation boundary and evidence pattern but tailor artifact kinds.

Steps.Title: Capture change demand and human acceptance boundary
Steps.Subtitle: AI work starts from a human-owned contract
Steps.Notes: Normalize the requested change into a bounded problem statement, value target, exclusions, and human acceptance criteria before any agent is engaged.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Feature request, defect, or improvement demand with business context.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Bounded change brief with explicit human acceptance boundary.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Intake brief and acceptance criteria map.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Product owner owns value boundary; no agent may redefine acceptance criteria alone.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not delegate ambiguous or ownerless tasks.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Product owner retains accountability for the change intent.
Architecture review confirms technical boundary.

Steps.Title: Define delegation boundary, allowed tools, and refusal conditions
Steps.Subtitle: The agent gets a sandbox, not a blank check
Steps.Notes: Translate the human change brief into a precise delegation contract that states what the agent may touch, what it must refuse, and which evidence it must produce.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Bounded change brief, repository context, data-sensitivity map, and tool inventory.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Approved delegation contract for agent execution.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Delegation contract and refusal boundary note.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Solution architect and AI safety reviewer define safe task decomposition; model-risk approver reviews autonomy fit for sensitive domains.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: If the delegation boundary cannot be explained precisely, do not delegate.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Delegate
BranchOutcomes.Description: The task can be delegated under stated constraints.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Human only
BranchOutcomes.Description: The task stays human-executed because safe delegation criteria are not met.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Architecture owner defines safe technical boundary.
AI safety review is required.
Model-risk review becomes required for sensitive change classes.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Project structure context brief
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by delegated agents and reviewers so they stay aligned on the same project node, directory, dependencies, and downstream artifact plan.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture the originating project-structure node, resolved working directory, touched modules or routes, dependency boundaries, and downstream artifact expectations.

Steps.Title: Run delegated execution and capture full trace
Steps.Subtitle: Every automated move must stay reproducible
Steps.Notes: Execute the delegated work, capture tool calls and outputs, and preserve the trace so later reviewers can understand what the agent actually did.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Delegation contract, prompt package, repository workspace, and allowed tools.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Draft change output plus full execution trace.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Execution trace pack, generated diff, and intermediate reasoning artifacts permitted by policy.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Software engineer supervises the lane; AI safety reviewer may halt execution when boundary breaches appear.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Stop immediately if the agent attempts disallowed files, tools, or data domains.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Engineer remains accountable for supervised execution.
Safety reviewer monitors boundary adherence.
Architect remains fallback for design ambiguity.

Steps.Title: Evaluate outputs against benchmark and acceptance evidence
Steps.Subtitle: A polished answer is not enough
Steps.Notes: Run deterministic checks, benchmark tasks, and human review prompts to determine whether the agent output actually satisfies the bounded acceptance criteria.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Generated diff, execution trace, acceptance criteria, test harness, and benchmark cases.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Evaluation report with pass/fail evidence and required rework.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Benchmark report, test evidence, and evaluator notes.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: AI evaluation lead owns measurement quality; QA lead reviews reproducibility and adequacy of tests.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not infer correctness from style, brevity, or model confidence.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Evaluation stewardship remains explicit.
QA validates reproducibility.
Engineer reviews implementation realism.

Steps.Title: Review safety, security, and residual risk
Steps.Subtitle: The output must be acceptable, not merely functional
Steps.Notes: Assess whether the agent-assisted output changes trust boundaries, introduces insecure patterns, or requires residual-risk ownership before merge.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Evaluation report, execution trace, code diff, and sensitive-scope map.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Approved, held, or rejected merge recommendation.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Safety/security approval record with residual risk statement.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Security reviewer and model-risk approver may block merge; release approver owns final risk acceptance for guarded lanes.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not merge when control impact is ambiguous.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Approved
BranchOutcomes.Description: The output may proceed to controlled merge.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Rework
BranchOutcomes.Description: The output must be revised or re-evaluated before merge.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Security review remains required.
Model-risk review remains explicit for guarded autonomy.
Controlled merge approval stays human.

Steps.Title: Merge under control and capture learning signal
Steps.Subtitle: Traceability does not end at approval
Steps.Notes: Perform the controlled merge, preserve trace references, and record what should change in prompts, benchmarks, or delegation policy next time.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Approved merge note, trace pack, evaluated diff, and rollout instructions if applicable.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Merged change with traceable evidence and improvement actions.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Merge note, trace references, and improvement backlog.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Software engineer performs the merge; AI evaluation lead captures benchmark improvement; product owner reviews value fit if needed.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not lose traceability between approved artifact and merged change.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Merge remains human-owned.
Evaluation lead records improvement signal.
Product review is required for customer-visible scope shifts.

Steps.Title: Keep delivery human-owned and close delegation request
Steps.Subtitle: Unsafe delegation becomes an explicit human handoff
Steps.Notes: Record why delegation was refused, preserve the human-owned boundary decision, and close the agent lane without pretending automated execution happened.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Closed delegation request with clear human follow-up ownership.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Delegation refusal note and handoff summary.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Product owner and solution architect confirm that the work remains human-executed.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not reopen an agent lane until the delegation boundary is redesigned explicitly.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Product owner accepts the human-only path.
Architecture owner confirms the delegation boundary remains closed.

Steps.Title: Capture rework decision and stop the merge lane
Steps.Subtitle: Rejected output must exit through a typed decision
Steps.Notes: Preserve the rework decision, residual concerns, and required next actions so the change can be revised deliberately instead of drifting through an implicit retry loop.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Safety and security review result with explicit rework findings.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Closed merge attempt with a typed rework directive.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Rework decision record and next-step note.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Security reviewer and release approver jointly define what must change before re-entry.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not treat rework as approved-by-delay; the merge lane stays closed until a new review cycle starts.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Security owner records the blocking reason.
Release approver confirms the merge lane stays closed.

LocalRoles.Summary: Owner for AI change evaluation design, benchmark selection, and evidence integrity.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Ensure AI-assisted work is judged using explicit evaluation criteria rather than optimism about model capability.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A technically rigorous evaluator for AI-assisted delivery or AI-enabled product changes.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Owner for AI change evaluation design, benchmark selection, and evidence integrity.
LocalRoles.SeniorityBand: Senior ML evaluation or quality leadership
KnowledgeRequirements: Ability to define evaluation tasks, benchmark coverage, and pass/fail thresholds for AI-assisted change work.
Knowledge of model behavior variability, failure patterns, and measurement caveats.
Understanding of dataset representativeness, leakage risk, and annotation quality.
Ability to separate convenience metrics from decision-grade evidence.
Knowledge of how human review and automated evaluation should complement each other.
Ability to document refusal or containment conditions for unsafe model output.
ExperienceRequirements: Has designed or reviewed evaluation plans for an AI-enabled feature or workflow.
Has interpreted benchmark or qualitative evaluation results in a release decision context.
Has caught misleading evaluation setups such as leakage, cherry-picking, or unrepresentative samples.
Has collaborated with product, engineering, and safety stakeholders on evaluation scope.
Has updated evaluation logic after observing production drift or blind spots.
DecisionRights: Approve evaluation scope and adequacy for AI-related change.
Reject evidence sets that are not decision-grade.
Escalate when measurement uncertainty is too high for delegated release approval.
Require explicit human review where automated evaluation cannot justify confidence.
CollaborationExpectations: Collaborate with AI safety, model risk, product, and engineering roles.
Make evaluation assumptions visible to decision-makers.
Protect evidence integrity when delivery pressure encourages shortcutting.
Feed production observations back into evaluation design.
AntiPatterns: Treating anecdotal good examples as proof of readiness.
Using metrics without explaining the dataset and test shape behind them.
Approving AI output quality without reviewing harmful failure modes.
Ignoring model or prompt changes that invalidate prior benchmarks.
FitnessEvidence: Evaluation plans with explicit scope, thresholds, and limits.
Benchmark results consumed successfully in governance decisions.
Evidence of catching misleading or incomplete AI evidence.

LocalRoles.Summary: Specialist reviewer for prompt, model-behavior, and misuse-resistant delivery controls.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Assess whether the AI-assisted workflow or AI-enabled output path has enough safety constraints and refusal logic for intended use.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A specialist in practical AI safety controls and failure containment.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Specialist reviewer for prompt, model-behavior, and misuse-resistant delivery controls.
LocalRoles.SeniorityBand: Senior AI safety or applied ML security specialist
KnowledgeRequirements: Knowledge of prompt design risk, prompt injection, jailbreak patterns, unsafe completion modes, and content-boundary controls.
Ability to assess whether refusal, escalation, and human-oversight conditions are real and enforceable.
Understanding of model provenance, tool-use risk, retrieval contamination, and output validation gaps.
Ability to review system prompts, evaluation prompts, and execution policies critically.
Knowledge of safety logging, red-team patterns, and incident response for AI misuse or harmful output.
Ability to align safety recommendations with delivery reality without weakening required control points.
ExperienceRequirements: Has reviewed AI workflows, prompts, or tool-using agents for safety and misuse risk.
Has identified unsafe prompt or policy assumptions before production use.
Has collaborated with engineers to implement or refine refusal and escalation controls.
Has supported red-team, tabletop, or incident work involving AI misuse scenarios.
Has documented safety decisions in a way usable by release governance.
DecisionRights: Approve or reject AI safety adequacy for covered use cases.
Require stronger refusal, guardrail, or validation controls before release.
Escalate high-risk misuse patterns to model risk approver and security stakeholders.
Set conditions for monitored or limited-scope rollout where appropriate.
CollaborationExpectations: Work with evaluation, product, security, and implementation roles.
Review actual prompts and execution traces rather than abstract descriptions only.
Help convert vague safety concern into implementable controls.
Participate in post-release review when harmful behavior is observed.
AntiPatterns: Assuming generic model provider safeguards cover the actual workflow risk.
Approving safety without reading prompts, tools, or evaluation traces.
Treating human review as magic without staffing or workflow reality.
Overfocusing on theoretical attacks while ignoring realistic misuse paths.
FitnessEvidence: Actionable safety reviews tied to concrete controls.
Examples of prevented unsafe rollout due to review findings.
Evidence of prompt/control improvements after review.
Cross-functional understanding of safety conditions created by the role.

LocalRoles.Summary: Decision authority for whether model-originated uncertainty is acceptable for the intended use.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Accept, conditionally accept, or reject AI-related change exposure based on model behavior risk and control coverage.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A senior risk owner combining product, security, compliance, and ML judgment.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Decision authority for whether model-originated uncertainty is acceptable for the intended use.
LocalRoles.SeniorityBand: Senior AI governance or risk leadership
KnowledgeRequirements: Ability to reason about failure modes, misuse, drift, opacity, and human-oversight limits for AI systems or AI-assisted workflows.
Knowledge of risk acceptance, conditional approval, and compensating-control design in AI contexts.
Understanding of where model uncertainty is tolerable versus unacceptable for the business or user.
Ability to weigh evaluation evidence, safety review, and operational controls together.
Knowledge of provenance, model versioning, and prompt/change governance implications.
Ability to articulate decision boundaries and review conditions in auditable language.
ExperienceRequirements: Has approved or rejected higher-risk AI usage or AI-enabled change proposals.
Has worked with security, compliance, product, and engineering on AI governance decisions.
Has handled exceptions or conditional approvals tied to control gaps.
Has reviewed production or near-production evidence of AI failure or misuse.
Has translated abstract AI risk into practical release conditions.
DecisionRights: Authorize, conditionally authorize, or reject AI-related release progression.
Require additional controls such as human review, throttling, or narrow scope.
Escalate when residual model risk exceeds delegated tolerance.
Set review expiry or re-validation conditions for approved usage.
CollaborationExpectations: Coordinate with evaluation lead, AI safety reviewer, product owner, and compliance roles.
State explicit operating conditions for approval decisions.
Ensure downstream teams understand approval limits and monitoring expectations.
Review follow-up signals after initial deployment or process adoption.
AntiPatterns: Approving because the AI output looks useful in demos.
Using generic AI policy language without concrete operating conditions.
Treating human oversight as sufficient when no one is realistically able to review the output properly.
FitnessEvidence: Auditable AI approval decisions with explicit conditions.
Evidence of rejecting or narrowing unsafe use cases.
Cross-functional trust in the role’s risk framing.
Re-validation or monitoring requirements captured and followed.

LocalArtifacts.Summary: Detailed AI evaluation report covering task set, scoring method, blind spots, and observed failures.
LocalArtifacts.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for AI approval, later re-validation, and incident/quality review while the evaluated model or prompt context remains materially similar.
LocalArtifacts.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must explain dataset shape, threshold logic, and known blind spots.

LocalArtifacts.Summary: Trace pack containing prompt, response, tool-use, and reviewer notes for sampled AI-assisted execution.
LocalArtifacts.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for AI safety review, audit, and later comparative evaluation within authorized audiences only.
LocalArtifacts.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must protect sensitive content and include enough context to interpret the sample correctly.

LocalChecklists.Summary: Checks whether AI delegation boundaries, refusal logic, and human-oversight assumptions are explicit before AI-assisted execution proceeds.
LocalChecklists.EntryCriteria: An AI-assisted step or AI-generated output path is proposed for real process use.
LocalChecklists.ExitCriteria: Delegation boundary, review obligations, and stop conditions are explicit and staffed.
Checks: Allowed and forbidden task types are documented.
Required human review points are explicit.
Prompt package and model identity are versioned.
Refusal and escalation behavior are defined.
Evaluation evidence exists for the intended use boundary.

LocalValidations.Summary: Confirms the workflow does not delegate materially sensitive judgment beyond the approved boundary.
LocalValidations.PassCriteria: Delegated tasks match the approved use boundary and required human checkpoints are intact.
LocalValidations.FailCriteria: Workflow silently extends AI autonomy beyond the reviewed scope or removes required human oversight.
LocalValidations.EscalationRule: Escalate immediately and suspend AI-assisted execution for the affected step.

LocalPrompts.Summary: Prompt scaffold for concise AI risk decisions with explicit operating conditions.
RefusalConditions: Refuse to recommend approval if approved scope and forbidden scope are not both explicit.
